name: netdust-gates
description: 0.13.1: a composer.json of type wordpress-muplugin is a WordPress project for the Global Constraints; the WordPress pack says a package closes on composer gate and ships by tag, and asks a route an agent will operate to declare `ability`, verified by the task that touches such a route, running wp-abilities-verify in runtime mode on its own DDEV, its reviewer reading the quote. Eval cases wp-pack-on-muplugin-package, wp-route-declares-ability. 0.13.0: the hunt, built in — every shake-out with a browser flow has shakeout-qa explore once, in its sweep, on the dev site with the browser it already drives: three to five charters, one surface from one posture (first-time visitor, numbers and copy, odd input, state after reload, error paths), about twenty actions each. A finding is a bug only when its Playwright repro fails on its assertion; a bug on a surface the diff does not touch is a not-ours line for Stefan and never blocks the close; rejected findings are listed for him to overrule. bin/shakeout-check.py requires a `Hunt: <n> charters · <c> confirmed · <x> not ours · <r> rejected` tally beside any browser row, or `Hunt: 0 charters — <why>` when the hunt could not run; not ours only when the diff provably misses the surface — in doubt, it is ours. On trial: five hunts in a row with nothing confirmed and it comes out. Replaces 0.12.0's e2e-tool version, which no project had opted into. 0.12.0: the hunt via tester.army's e2e — on a project carrying e2e.config.ts, shakeout-qa's sweep runs tester.army's e2e explore (npx e2e guide bug-bash) with once per shake-out, charters over the feature's Test map flows and the diff with upstream's postures, local only (--target the dev site; explorer output under .e2e/, never committed); a finding is a bug only when its Playwright repro fails on its assertion, then a fail row like any other; charters and rejected findings sit under the manifest table as plain lines, and Stefan can overrule a rejection at the screenshot yield. 0.11.0: two sessions — a planned feature runs as a reviewer (the session Stefan talked to) and a coder session in its own worktree, started by netdust-core's pair recipe in herdr or as one background subagent outside it; the brief opens Role: coder, the coder asks its reviewer and never Stefan, and the execution-mode choice is no longer a stop; /feature-review reads the plan at the reviewed head. Eval cases two-session-handoff and coder-brief-no-recursion; run-evals.py gives every case its own environment (no inherited HERDR_* or CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_*, a dead socket) and a stub herdr that shadows the real one. 0.10.0: the Test map — netdust-gates:test-mapping writes a plan section with one row per unit (seam · tier · file · command · e2e flows) and cuts the tasks to those units; RED-first stays for the denial test and the Close fix pass; shakeout-qa, plan-reviewer, threat-modeling and test-pruner read it instead of deciding; the growth rule reads "never a plan section a skill does not own". Eval case unit-cut-plan. 0.9.1: docs follow the current flow — netdust-gates owns the policy and hooks, netdust-devops the branches and deploy; the Close runs gate → review → fix → shakeout → promote; feature artifacts live in specs/<feature>/. 0.9.0: /feature-review honours REVIEW_LEVEL (low · full · ultra, which checks collisions with staging before landing) and ends with a Findings line; /review-fix <feature> turns a saved review into follow-up commits on the branch, the way a PR's review comments become commits, and keeps the record in specs/<feature>/review.md. 0.8.1: /shakeout on a branch with no spec derives the changed surfaces from the diff, explores them, proposes specs/<feature>/flows.md and stops for Stefan's approval; shakeout-qa then drives only the approved flows, so a hand-started feature reaches make e2e too. 0.8.0: /feature-review runs the reviewers on a feature (plan or none) or on where staging's features meet, and reports back; Close step 3 is make review name=<feature>. Eval case close-calls-make-review. 0.7.0: the plan is the feature. A spec split into sub-projects stays at specs/<topic>/spec.md; each plan is specs/<feature>/plan.md with a Spec: line, one plan per feature/<feature> branch, with no dependency declared between plans. /plan-review <topic> reviews the whole set in one dispatch, and plan-reviewer judges the cut: too broad, artificially split, or a requirement owned by no plan or by two. Close ends with the branch pushed and make promote handed to Stefan; the feature shake-out writes the checks, and make e2e env=staging is the gate ship waits for (devops 0.7.7). Eval cases: spec-splits-into-plans, plan-review-flags-artificial-split, close-hands-over-promote. 0.4.3: the Stop hook never touches git — it writes memory/ and tasks/, and keeps its watermark sidecar out of git status through the checkout's own .git/info/exclude; no more .gitignore edits or auto-capture commits on whatever branch was checked out (a deploy rung included). Committing memory is the author's job, on a feature branch. 0.4.2: the WordPress pack is enforceable as text — each Global Constraint names its evidence (a quoted command or the review that owns it), a red-flags table travels verbatim into the plan, and the whole-branch review on WordPress is joined by ntdst-drift-reviewer; eval case wp-constraints-carry-evidence. 0.4.1: the plan-review floor is gone — no plan state, reviewed or not, blocks a code edit; /plan-review stays a practice for a plan that exists. 0.4.0: two on-demand reviews, both report-only until Stefan approves. /session-review <feature> — a read-only session-reviewer checks the task reports, rulings, plan and diff against the real source on six dimensions (correctness, architecture, simplicity, core fit via core-fit.md on WordPress, tests, user-facing consequences), security-sentinel when it says so. /session-learn [session] — a read-only session-learner reads a transcript (superpowers' context-safety and path:line discipline) for Stefan's corrections, gates fired or bypassed, skills missed, rulings and failed premises, and proposes lessons with eval cases; superpowers-caused findings route to superpowers:diagnosing-superpowers. 0.3.0: the checks registry — every shake-out registers what it leaves in specs/CHECKS.md: the flows it drove as @e2e (make e2e env=staging, the proof after a deploy or a plugin update) and a fixture-free, read-only @smoke check per surface (make smoke, production too). shakeout-check fails a driven feature with no e2e or no smoke row, a missing test, a test without its tier's tag; /shakeout reads the registry first. 0.2.0: /plan-review — a fresh plan-reviewer subagent ground-truths the plan's premises against the source before Stefan reads it, files specs/<f>/plan-review.md naming the plan's blob, and the guard refuses product code while a plan open on this branch has no review of its current text. Netdust's software-delivery policy over superpowers: standards injected into the spec and plan, verification by executables (make gate, the shake-out manifest check), authority hooks. Pilot on netdust.be; replaces netdust-agent there and never runs beside it.
